title: It Ends
review: Car {Aniara}. {Stand By Me} for existentialists. True cosmic terror. {The Blair Witch Project} for Gen Z. As I was watching this, I had already written a tentative 10 in my notes, but the very last scene had me changing it down to a 9. The concept and execution is so good, and with such an obviously low budget, it seems like a movie that could have become a viral sensation with a little more luck and a broader release. There's still time for a slow burn into cult classic status. It has so far made back 10 times its budget, but compare that to the inferior {Backrooms} (40 times its budget), and the possibly superior {Obsession} (1000 times its budget), and they probably feel like they missed out on the real jackpot.
spoilers: I'm not sure if I liked the ending. The end of the road made things a little more surprising and fun, turning the title of the movie into the setup for a visual gag when he sees the sign. It gave James a reason to turn back and try to reunite with his friends; a glimmer of hope, that there will be one more future event to look forward to. Ending as he begins on this mission left me hoping that he succeeds. But... Imagine the sheer terror of infinite nothingness. Imagine if this film faded to black really slowly as James became more and more twisted and manic alone in the car, never seeing an end to the road, and torturing himself via a sunk cost fallacy of his own making. Pulling off a true endless road would have been much scarier, but harder to execute in earnest.
